barriers.description: Pre-prepared stress scripts were perceived by teens as inauthentic and even 'insulting', forcing researchers to abandon them and ask teens to craft their own stories.
barriers.justification: This negative reaction undermined trust and authenticity, hindering the researchers' ability to manage user understanding and to facilitate authentic participation and iteration in role-play interaction studies.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, the first time we presented this script, a few teens immediately commented in writing on the script that they found this script was “insulting” and “fake.” Although based in teen data, our script did not meet the teens’ need for an authentic story during role play and interaction.

barriers.description: Creating relationships with stakeholders and users in participatory research was time consuming, limiting how quickly researchers could engage and iterate.
barriers.justification: The time-intensive nature of relationship-building constrained the team's capacity to facilitate user involvement at scale and to sustain ongoing user-centred iteration and evaluation activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, as is often true in participatory research, the process of creating relationships with stakeholders and users can be time consuming.

barriers.description: Conducting studies 'in the wild' introduced many uncontrollable situations that could cause studies to fail despite researcher flexibility.
barriers.justification: Unpredictable field conditions impeded the team's ability to reliably plan and execute user research, which hindered understanding context of use, conducting evaluations, and performing iterative design cycles.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, conducting studies in the wild provides huge benefits for contextual validity, but also allows for an unlimited number of uncontrollable situations. Maintaining flexibility within design can be helpful, but even then there is still potential for studies to fail in the wild.

barriers.description: Communicating and disseminating novel participatory methods to the engineering community was difficult and time intensive.
barriers.justification: This external communication burden limited the team's ability to coordinate multidisciplinary collaboration and to integrate participatory-method feedback into broader engineering practices, slowing adoption and iterative refinement across stakeholders.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Finally, although often much appreciated, communicating and disseminating new, participatory iterations of commonly used methods to an engineering community can be difﬁcult and time intensive.
